interpretations.answer: The estimated average treatment effect of t on y ranges from 4.94 to 5.16 outcome units. Design d1e8ae99c4041 estimates an effect of 5.137751952370555 (95% CI: 4.934846069047842, 5.3601749844607784) by adjusting for 'c' and 'x' using propensity score weighting. Design dd19897b8bbe5 estimates an effect of 5.1596960800161975 (95% CI: 4.933498908594317, 5.434866464881059) by adjusting for 'c' using propensity score weighting. Design dd268c9025c41 estimates an effect of 4.936558041190057 (95% CI: 4.74666920946521, 5.122205819274052) by adjusting for 'c' using a general linear model.
caveats: All designs show a soft flag for baseline imbalance in 'c' before adjustment, with a standardized mean difference of 1.322 (check:d1e8ae99c4041.1_vs_0.balance.c, check:dd19897b8bbe5.1_vs_0.balance.c, check:dd268c9025c41.1_vs_0.balance.c).

Designs d1e8ae99c4041 and dd19897b8bbe5 have a soft flag for stratification support, indicating that propensity stratification would retain 642 of 1200 rows (check:d1e8ae99c4041.1_vs_0.stratification_support) and 879 of 1200 rows (check:dd19897b8bbe5.1_vs_0.stratification_support) respectively, but this is a hypothetical screen for an excluded estimator.

Sensitivity analysis for d1e8ae99c4041 shows the estimate ranges from -1.29 to 4.84 (sensitivity:d1e8ae99c4041.1_vs_0.add_unobserved_common_cause.range) under simulated unobserved confounders, and for dd19897b8bbe5, it ranges from -1.25 to 4.87 (sensitivity:dd19897b8bbe5.1_vs_0.add_unobserved_common_cause.range).

All designs passed placebo treatment refuters (falsification:d1e8ae99c4041.1_vs_0.placebo_treatment_refuter.passed, falsification:dd19897b8bbe5.1_vs_0.placebo_treatment_refuter.passed, falsification:dd268c9025c41.1_vs_0.placebo_treatment_refuter.passed) and data subset refuters (falsification:d1e8ae99c4041.1_vs_0.data_subset_refuter.passed, falsification:dd19897b8bbe5.1_vs_0.data_subset_refuter.passed, falsification:dd268c9025c41.1_vs_0.data_subset_refuter.passed), and graph independence tests (falsification:d1e8ae99c4041.1_vs_0.graph_independences.passed, falsification:dd19897b8bbe5.1_vs_0.graph_independences.passed, falsification:dd268c9025c41.1_vs_0.graph_independences.passed).
comparisons: Design d1e8ae99c4041 (propensity score weighting, adjusting for c and x) and design dd19897b8bbe5 (propensity score weighting, adjusting for c) yield similar estimates, while design dd268c9025c41 (general linear model, adjusting for c) provides a slightly lower estimate.

The primary difference in assumptions splitting the designs is whether 'x' is included in the adjustment set for unconfoundedness: design d1e8ae99c4041 assumes unconfoundedness given 'c' and 'x' (design:d1e8ae99c4041.assumptions), whereas designs dd19897b8bbe5 and dd268c9025c41 assume unconfoundedness given only 'c' (design:dd19897b8bbe5.assumptions, design:dd268c9025c41.assumptions).
